comparison: Both evaluate claims C54-C63 about two-aster exclusion zones and fluid flow analysis. OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with strong quantitative evidence, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN, specifically critiquing that 'tracking of fluid flows is hard to see and better quantifications/analyses would lead to stronger conclusions.'

Both evaluate claims C81-C83 about pharmacological perturbation experiments. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and statistical significance, while peer reviewers accept the perturbation experiments as supporting evidence for the pushing model.

Both evaluate claims C105-C106 about differences between explants and intact embryos. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of system limitations, while peer reviewers accept this as valid contextualization rather than a fundamental flaw.

Both evaluate the experimental system (C26-C30). OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED with clear documentation, while peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, noting the explant system enabled accurate measurements despite being 'artificial.' Peer result R6 also includes C25 and C100 not in OpenEval R1.

OpenEval R13 evaluates claims C91-C94, C99 about modeling one and two asters, finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R5 evaluates C91-C99 (including C95-C98 from OpenEval R14), also finding them SUPPORTED and praising the modeling as 'powerful' and 'a notable achievement.'

OpenEval R14 evaluates claims C95-C98 about modeling higher-order aster arrangements, finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R5 covers these same claims within a broader evaluation (C91-C99) and also finds them SUPPORTED, accepting the modeling results.

Both evaluate speculative molecular mechanisms. OpenEval R19 finds claims C114-C117, C122 UNCERTAIN, noting they are not directly tested. Peer R7 evaluates C111-C122 as UNCERTAIN, explicitly identifying as a weakness that 'molecular mechanisms underlying aster repulsion remain unexplored.'

OpenEval R2 evaluates single aster dynamics (C31-C38, C46) as SUPPORTED with strong quantitative data. Peer R1 includes these claims within a much broader evaluation (C4, C31-C49, C84-C86, C101-C103, C107) and finds them SUPPORTED, praising the pushing force evidence as 'a major strength.'

OpenEval R3 evaluates microtubule distribution claims C39-C43 as SUPPORTED with appropriate quantitative analysis. Peer R1 includes these claims in a broader evaluation and also finds them SUPPORTED as part of the evidence for pushing forces.

OpenEval R4 evaluates microtubule buckling observations (C44-C45, C47, C111-C113) as SUPPORTED evidence for pushing forces. Peer R1 includes C44-C45, C47 in their broader evaluation and finds them SUPPORTED as part of the major strength of pushing force evidence.

OpenEval R5 evaluates the main conclusion about repulsive potential (C49, C79, C101, C107-C108) as SUPPORTED by collective evidence. Peer R1 includes C49, C101, C107 in their evaluation and finds them SUPPORTED, affirming this as a major strength.

OpenEval R7 evaluates two-aster positioning and force balance (C64-C68, C80, C102) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 evaluates overlapping claims C64-C74, C79-C80, C87-C90 as UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning statistical rigor: 'it is not clear that the acceleration is significant and no statistical test is provided.'

OpenEval R8 evaluates aster relaxation dynamics (C69-C71) as SUPPORTED with quantitative data. Peer R3 includes these claims in a broader evaluation (C64-C74, C79-C80, C87-C90) rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about statistical testing of acceleration effects.

OpenEval R9 evaluates exponential decay of repulsive force (C72-C74, C77) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C72-C74 in their evaluation rated UNCERTAIN, questioning the statistical rigor of the two-aster dynamics analysis.

OpenEval R11 evaluates laser ablation experiments (C84-C86) as SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer R1 includes these claims in their broader evaluation and finds them SUPPORTED as part of the major strength demonstrating pushing forces.

OpenEval R12 evaluates additional ablation experiments (C87-C90) as SUPPORTED and consistent with the repulsive force model. Peer R3 includes these claims in their evaluation rated UNCERTAIN due to concerns about statistical testing.

OpenEval R15 evaluates the ~35 µm interaction range (C103-C104) as SUPPORTED by collective observations. Peer R1 includes C103 in their broader evaluation and finds it SUPPORTED as part of the repulsive potential evidence.

OpenEval R4 includes claims C111-C113 about pushing forces and buckling, finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates C111-C122 (broader molecular mechanism claims) as UNCERTAIN, noting the molecular mechanisms remain unexplored.

OpenEval R20 evaluates claims C118-C119 about molecular-level properties as SUPPORTED by citations, though noting C119 is not directly tested. Peer R7 includes these in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, identifying lack of molecular mechanism identification as a weakness.

OpenEval R21 evaluates claims C120-C121 acknowledging limitations about ATP-independent mechanisms as SUPPORTED (appropriate acknowledgment). Peer R7 includes these in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting the molecular mechanisms remain unexplored.

OpenEval R16 evaluates speculative mechanistic explanations (C33-C34, C47-C48) as UNCERTAIN, noting they lack experimental validation. Peer R1 includes C47 in their broader SUPPORTED evaluation focused on the phenomenological observations rather than mechanistic details.

OpenEval R22 evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C25, C50-C53, C75-C76, C100) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R6 includes only C25-C30, C100 in their evaluation of the experimental system, also finding them SUPPORTED.
OpenEval R18 evaluates claims C109-C110 about comparison with other systems as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific comparative context claims.
